sources.entry: Wayback - A self-hosted toolkit for archiving webpages to the Internet Archive, archive.today, IPFS, and local file systems. GPL-3.0 Go

summary.one_liner: Wayback is a self-hosted web archiving tool that captures webpages to the Internet Archive, archive.today, IPFS, and local disk, and can be driven through chat platforms and a CLI.
summary.what_it_does: Wayback captures web content and preserves it in several destinations, including the Internet Archive, archive.today, IPFS, Telegraph, and local file storage. It provides a built-in CLI (`wayback`) and can run as a daemon that accepts requests through IRC, Matrix, Telegram, Discord, Mastodon, Twitter, and XMPP bots. It can batch multiple URLs for archiving and publish results to a Telegram channel, Mastodon, or GitHub Issues. The README also describes a search and playback service for retrieving archived pages, a Tor Hidden Service or local web entry option, Prometheus metrics, and downloading streaming media via FFmpeg.
use_cases: archive webpages to the Internet Archive and archive.today
archive links shared in chat rooms via bots
save offline copies of web pages to disk
publish archived links to a Telegram channel or Mastodon
how_to_run: sudo apt install wayback (after adding the wabarc APT repository)
notable: Archives one URL to several targets at once: Internet Archive, archive.today, IPFS, Telegraph, and local disk
Chat-bot daemon interfaces for IRC, Matrix, Telegram, Discord, Mastodon, Twitter, and XMPP
Can be served as a Tor Hidden Service for privacy
Packaged for Snap, APT, and RPM alongside GitHub Releases
caveats: Streaming media archiving requires FFmpeg to be installed separately
The README points to external documentation for the full setup guide and does not detail every configuration step
Bot and publishing integrations each need their own account credentials set up (not detailed in the README)
